statement: In the small trials of MDMA-assisted therapy outside PTSD read for this page (anxiety with a life-threatening illness, 13 on MDMA and 5 on placebo; social anxiety in autistic adults, 8 and 4; major depression, 12 open-label; couples, 6 and 8 couples open-label), no serious adverse event was attributed to MDMA and no participant stopped treatment because of side effects. During sessions MDMA was followed more often than placebo by jaw clenching (11 of 13 vs 1 of 5), thirst (11 of 13 vs 2 of 5), sweating (9 of 13 vs 0 of 5) and headache (8 of 13 vs 1 of 5), and in autistic adults by anxiety (6 of 8 vs 1 of 4); in the following week by fatigue and needing more sleep (12 of 13 each vs 3 and 2 of 5); blood pressure, pulse and temperature rose during sessions without needing treatment. Suicidal ideation was recorded as an adverse event in 2 of 8 autistic adults on MDMA (and 1 of 4 on placebo), and worsening suicidal ideation in 4 to 6 of 12 people with depression; 2 of those 12 received benzodiazepines and zopiclone for anxiety and insomnia after dosing. Side effects were mostly collected as spontaneous reports or by the treating therapists, and with at most 13 people on MDMA per trial, rare or delayed harms could not be detected. Certainty: very low. Status: replicated.
plain: In small trials of MDMA therapy for problems other than PTSD, no one had a serious side effect from MDMA. Short-lived effects such as a tight jaw, thirst, sweating, headache and tiredness were common. These trials were too small to show rare harms.
population: Adults in published trials of MDMA-assisted therapy outside PTSD that were read in full: anxiety with a life-threatening illness, social anxiety in autistic adults, major depressive disorder, and couples in which one partner had PTSD
exposure: MDMA in two (occasionally three) supervised sessions within psychotherapy
comparator: Inactive placebo with the same psychotherapy in two trials; none in the open-label studies
outcome: Adverse events, expected reactions, vital signs and suicidal ideation during and after MDMA sessions
magnitude: Anxiety with a life-threatening illness (MDMA 13, placebo 5): during sessions jaw clenching 11 vs 1, thirst 11 vs 2, dry mouth 9 vs 1, perspiration 9 vs 0, headache 8 vs 1; in the next 7 days fatigue 12 vs 3, needing more sleep 12 vs 2, insomnia 9 vs 2; peak temperature 37.3 vs 36.9 °C. Autistic adults (8, 4): anxiety 6 vs 1, difficulty concentrating 5 vs 1; suicidal ideation 2 vs 1; peak systolic pressure, pulse and temperature higher on MDMA (maximum pulse 114, maximum temperature 37.7 °C). Depression (12, open-label): 46 adverse events in 10 participants, none serious; worsening suicidal ideation in 4 to 6. Veteran couples (8 dosed): headache 6 of 8 within 7 days, raised blood pressure 3 of 8. Serious adverse events attributed to MDMA: none among the 58 people given MDMA in these five studies (counting the 5 placebo participants of the life-threatening-illness trial who later took MDMA open-label).

evidence.extracted: During the two blinded sessions, MDMA (13) vs placebo (5): jaw clenching 11 vs 1, thirst 11 vs 2, dry mouth 9 vs 1, perspiration 9 vs 0, headache 8 vs 1; in the following 7 days fatigue 12 vs 3, needing more sleep 12 vs 2, insomnia 9 vs 2; reactions decreased over the week.

Treatment-emergent adverse events infrequent and nearly equal between groups; serious events only from cancer recurrence or progression (one death about a year after stopping, unrelated to MDMA); only peak temperature differed (37.3 vs 36.9 °C); no serious suicidal ideation or behaviour; no discontinuation because of adverse effects related to MDMA.

evidence.locator: Results › Safety, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Tables 4 and 5
evidence.extracted: No serious adverse events; during sessions anxiety in 6 of 8 on MDMA vs 1 of 4 on placebo and difficulty concentrating 5 vs 1; one severe headache on MDMA; suicidal ideation as an adverse event in 2 of 8 vs 1 of 4, pre-existing in medical history; depressed mood 2 of 8 vs 0.

Mean peak systolic blood pressure (P = 0.021), pulse (P = 0.015) and temperature (P < 0.001) higher on MDMA; maximum pulse 114 bpm, maximum temperature 37.7 °C; no systolic pressure above 180 or diastolic above 110 mmHg; values back to pre-drug levels by session end.

46 adverse events in 10 of 12, 15 moderate and 31 mild, none serious, no discontinuations; most common headache, increased suicidal ideation and jaw muscle tightness; benzodiazepines and zopiclone for 2 participants after dosing; worsening intensity of suicidal ideation in 6 participants (12 events).
Suicidal ideation given as 33.3% in the comparison with MAPP1; adverse events were reported to the therapy team, which may have led to under-reporting.

No serious adverse events; every veteran had at least one treatment-emergent adverse event; headache 75.0%, feeling warm 37.5%, increased blood pressure 37.5%, nausea, decreased appetite and sadness 25.0% each within 7 days of an MDMA session; no high suicide risk on the C-SSRS.
All six couples completed the protocol; no serious adverse events; the most common reactions after MDMA sessions were diminished appetite, anxiety, headache and jaw tightness.

risk_of_bias.note: Spontaneous or therapist-recorded side effects; possible under-reporting.

grade.reasoning: A descriptive claim about what was recorded in these trials: starts low. Risk of bias one level: side effects were collected as spontaneous reports or by the treating therapists, which the depression trial's authors say may have led to under-reporting, and the counts of suicidal ideation differ within one paper; this could materially change the figures. Imprecision is not rated down separately because the claim gives counts and states that rare or delayed harms could not be detected. Status 'replicated': the same pattern of short-lived sympathomimetic and mood reactions, without serious adverse events attributed to MDMA, was recorded by independent teams in the United States and Norway. To be joined with the other reader's claim from the cross-indication reviews.
